single.rationale: Intapp shows exceptional fundamentals with 23% three-year revenue CAGR, 29% Cloud ARR growth, 120% cloud net revenue retention, and impressive operating leverage improvement (losses narrowing from -$99.5M to -$27.4M while FCF surged to $121.9M at 24% margin). The company serves sticky, premium clients in professional services with strong expansion economics, though high share dilution (10% YoY) and elevated valuation (6.5x EV/revenue) warrant deeper analysis of capital allocation and competitive positioning.

dropped.claim: Intapp presents a compelling case of improving unit economics with operating cash flow reaching $123.5M and 24.2% FCF margins while Cloud ARR grew 29% to $383.1M with 120% net revenue retention, demonstrating strong operational leverage in a high-margin SaaS business. However, three critical uncertainties warrant deeper investigation before conviction: first, management's explicit warning about ROI demonstration risk and its potential impact on net revenue retention lacks historical context on churn trends and competitive win rates; second, revenue growth deceleration to 17.1% YoY from a 22.8% three-year CAGR raises questions about organic momentum versus the TermSheet acquisition contribution; third, 10.1% annual share dilution materially offsets the improving per-share economics. The 120% Cloud NRR is encouraging but needs trend analysis, and understanding whether the revenue deceleration represents market saturation or temporary factors is essential for assessing the durability of the 24.2% FCF margins against continued 27.3% R&D intensity.
